text: The response converts 30 snakes into birds by multiplying by 12, the beetles eaten per bird, instead of by the 3 birds each snake eats, then multiplies by 12 again for beetles, so one rate is used twice and the birds-per-snake rate is never applied.

The response multiplies Keaton's 30-foot ladder by his twenty climbs but converts Reece's 26-foot ladder to inches only once, never multiplying by Reece's 15 climbs, so Reece's repeated climbing is omitted from the combined length.

The response ignores the stated $18 left over: it labels salary minus necessities as total expenses, derives its own leftover of 42 from that, and reports salary minus 42 as the tax, so the given remainder never enters the tax calculation.

The response encodes 'twenty days ago he had half his current practice' as P equals P over 2, an impossible equation, and then asserts x equals 2, instead of using the condition to express current practice as 40 days of daily practice before solving for the additional days.

The response computes the third of Frank's 36 apples that he sold and then treats those 12 sold apples as the amount he has left, instead of subtracting them from 36; Susan's half happens to equal her remainder, but Frank's does not.

The response omits Rockefeller's guns, uses one unknown for Grenada's whole stock as if it were each category count, splits the 6000 between the two bases and sets Rockefeller's total equal to Grenada's, instead of giving each of Grenada's three supply types an equal share of 6000.

The response triples the 6-month research and the 2-year expedition correctly, but when converting the second artifact's 18 months plus 6 years into years it writes 8.5 years, treating 18 months as 2.5 years, a unit-conversion error that inflates the total.

The response correctly sets up the deposit as half of the 14-day rental at $125 plus the $100 pet fee plus a 20% service fee, but never evaluates these expressions and prints four conflicting final lines, none of which follows from its own setup.

The response converts pounds to ounces with a factor of 1.16 ounces per pound instead of 16 ounces per pound, applying this wrong conversion to all three amounts, so each friend's fudge and the summed total in ounces are far too small.

The response claims to reverse the steps but treats the initial 143 cm board as the final length and subtracts both the 7 cm and 25 cm cuts from it, so its answer is a length after cutting rather than the length before the 7 cm cut that the question asks for.

The response repeats the cut-and-donate process four times, summing donations of 50, 25, 12.5 and 6.25 square inches, although the question says Fatima does this only 2 times, so two extra donation rounds are added to the total.

The response computes the number of $5 bracelets by dividing the 30-bracelet stock by the $5 price instead of dividing the $60 earned by $5, then ignores the given $60 revenue and sells all 30 bracelets again as $8 pairs instead of only the bracelets that remain.

The response halves the $1,000,000 price only twice, labelling the first halving as the price at age 20, although 30 years contain three 10-year periods, so it skips the halving between birth and age 10 and stops one halving short.

The response counts only the initial round on Saturday and drops the 10 additional rounds the team completed later that day, so Saturday contributes one 30-minute round instead of eleven, and the weekend total omits ten rounds.

The response correctly finds 22 yards needed and converts 7 feet to 7/3 yards, but evaluates 22 minus 7/3 as 22 2/3, a difference larger than the amount needed, and leaves the answer in yards although the question asks for feet.

The response subtracts the leaking time from the normal time, computing 3 minus 5 minutes, which reverses the order of the difference and makes the extra time negative; it then reports a negative value for how much longer 12 barrels take, contradicting its own closing sentence.

The response miscounts the guests: it lists Iris herself with her mother instead of her brother, and uses 3 aunts although the question gives 4, so only six aunt-or-uncle family units are counted and both the adults and their children are undercounted.

The response counts a full 15 videos for the fifth round, although on the final list Billy watches only up to the 5th suggestion, so the last round should contribute five videos instead of fifteen; the stopping condition stated in the question is ignored.

The response doubles the two-week total of 7 pounds and then adds the weekly 3 pounds of kale to it, treating a two-week quantity as a weekly one, instead of doubling the half-pound daily amount and scaling it to one week.

The response pools Monday's and Tuesday's situps against one total of 30, concluding the goal is already exceeded, although the question treats 30 as the daily goal and asks Shawna to also make up each day's shortfall, so Wednesday's own 30 and the missed situps are ignored.

The response correctly finds the occupied chairs but equates the number of attending members with the number of occupied chairs, ignoring that each occupied chair held two people, so the attendance is half of what the stated seating capacity implies.

The response subtracts the 5% overlap from each spray separately, giving 45% and 20%, so the shared germs are removed twice; counting the overlap once requires subtracting it a single time from the combined 75% killed.

The response correctly computes the weekly losses of each bird type and subtracts them from the 580 birds, but evaluates 580 minus 140 minus 56 minus 35 as 359, an execution error of ten in the final subtraction.

The response sets up total savings as 25 times 12 times 2 and plans to subtract the $400 repair, but never evaluates these expressions and reports 1100, a value inconsistent with its own setup; its final step even plans to subtract the $400 a second time.

The response correctly finds 30 sections left after the gift and 15 put in storage, but computes the sections kept as the original 40 minus the 15 stored, instead of the 30 remaining minus 15, so the 10 sections given to the friend are counted back in.

The response assigns every car exactly 4 tires and says this includes the spare, ignoring the condition that a quarter of the 16 cars have a spare tire included, so the extra tire on each of those cars is never counted.

The response treats the berry package prices as per-cup prices, multiplying 4 cups by $3.00 and by $5.00, although each package contains 2 cups; it also buys a separate 4-cup cream container for each quart although the two quarts need only 4 cups together.

The response correctly writes the fourth day as twice the first three days' total but evaluates (50 + 100 + 120) times 2 as 270, which is the undoubled sum, so the doubling is dropped in execution and the four-day total is understated.

The response divides the $120 profit by the $15 profit per book, which yields the number of books sold, and labels that result as the number of customers, ignoring that every customer buys 2 books; its own revenue-per-customer figure is never used.

The response multiplies each croissant price by 52 to get yearly spending but labels these as weekly amounts, then multiplies their sum by 52 weeks again, so the number of weeks is applied twice; the final product is also misevaluated.

The response divides the full weekly requirement of 14 cups by the 5 days that have already passed, ignoring the 8 cups Sarah has already eaten and the 2 days left in the week, so it answers a rate for elapsed days rather than the remaining need.

The response's only final-answer line, written before its reasoning, gives 14, which is Alexa's shoe size alone, although the following sentences correctly add Jasmine's 7 and Alexa's 14; the reported answer is an intermediate quantity rather than the combined size asked for.

The response scales yearly story pages to 12 weeks by multiplying 7800 by 12, instead of multiplying the 150 weekly pages by 12 weeks, so the pages become larger than a year's worth; it also omits the 1200-page novel from the paper count.

The response sets the break height to 12 minus 2 feet, as if the tip merely dropped by 2 feet, ignoring that the broken top segment hangs down from the break point, so the tip's height equals the break height minus the folded segment's length.

The response subtracts the dog's 2 eyes from the 22 that Oomyapeck eats, although those 22 are what remains after the dog's share, and then divides 22 eyes by 3 as if each eye were a fish, never converting eyes to fish at two eyes per fish.

The response subtracts only the kiwi and banana spending from the $50 and never deducts the $3.50 subway fare for each direction; it then divides the money by a per-apple price although apples are sold only in $14 bags of a dozen.

The response doubles only the first day's 5 seashells for the third day, although the question says the third day's count is twice the number found over the first two days combined, so the second day's 7 seashells are left out of the doubling.

The response treats the initial schedule of 10 hours travel, 3 hours stop, 10 hours travel and 1 hour stop as a repeating cycle and sums it as 14 hours instead of 24, although afterwards the ship breaks 1 hour per 11 hours of travel; its stop-time total is built on these false cycles.

The response correctly expresses the pixel count as 21 inches times 100 dots multiplied by 12 inches times 100 dots, but never evaluates these expressions and reports 24000, a number far from the product defined by its own setup.

The response correctly writes total earnings as 12 dollars times 8 haircuts plus 25 dollars times 5 styles, but never evaluates the products and reports 280, a total that contradicts the sum defined by its own expression.

The response sets one sixth of a day equal to 24 hours, the length of a whole day, instead of taking one sixth of 24 hours, so the reading time per book type and every page count are six times larger than the question's time budget allows.

The response sums only the $20000 bank loan and its 15% interest as Mike's total payment, omitting the part of the $35000 car price that he pays without borrowing, so the total excludes the non-loan portion of the price.

The response charges adult admission for all 10 people and then adds 4 half-price child tickets, although the 4 children are part of the 10, so the children are counted twice and the adult count should be the 10 people minus the children.

The response adds an invented material cost of $100 per table, labelled as a cost per plank, to the $3000 labor, although the question states labor as the only cost; this unstated expense reduces the computed profit.

The response correctly finds 15 white trucks among 90 vehicles and converts the probability to a percentage, but reports 16.67 without rounding to the nearest integer, although the question explicitly asks for the percentage rounded to a whole number.

The response starts from only 4 initial bottles, although Martha had 4 bottles in the refrigerator and another 4 in the pantry, so one storage location is dropped before the 5 purchased bottles are added and the 3 drunk are subtracted.

The response correctly prices the sports channels at $3 less than the movie channels, but its total monthly payment adds only the two channel packages and omits the $15 basic service that Jessica keeps paying, so one stated cost is never added.

The response correctly writes the tax as 200 times 0.15 and the total as 200 plus that tax, but never evaluates these expressions and reports 260, a total inconsistent with adding a 15% tax to the $200 price.

The response buys only 3 main meals, counting the co-workers but not Bret himself, although Bret and his 3 co-workers make four diners, so one meal is missing from the subtotal and from the base of the 20% tip.

The response states it will subtract the resale from the total cost of both rings, but subtracts the $5,000 resale only from the wife's $20,000 ring, leaving out the $10,000 Jim paid for the first ring, so its out-of-pocket total omits one purchase.

The response invents a current value by adding another $4000 to the purchase price, a doubling the question never states, and then triples this invented $8000 value, instead of taking three times the $4000 purchase price as the future value.

The response defines the four-subject total as the average plus the History score, which is twice the average, instead of the three actual scores plus the History score; it also reports 200, which does not equal even its own expression of two averages.

The response's only final-answer line, written before its reasoning, states 12, while the following steps correctly subtract the 31 badges of Hermione and Luna from the 83 total; the reported answer contradicts the result of its own correct computation.

After computing the starting current for all three units, the response adds one more 40A running current on top of it, although the minimum transformer load is set by the starting requirement alone, so an extra unit's running current is added without basis.

The response correctly sets up Monday's 40 times 6 and Tuesday's 20 times 10 m&ms and divides their total by 40 per pack, but never evaluates these expressions and reports 20 packs, a count inconsistent with its own setup.

The response sets up and solves the consecutive-age equation correctly for the youngest brother, but both its opening final-answer line and its closing sentence report 24, an unexplained value that contradicts its own derivation.

The response correctly writes the total as 6 vans times 10 students plus 4 minibusses times 24 students, but never evaluates the products and reports 108, a total inconsistent with the sum defined by its own expressions.

The response correctly finds the extra postage above standard rates but spreads it over all 4 letters, although only the 2 international letters carry the additional charge, so the per-letter international surcharge is understated by half.

The response sets the new enrollment to 5 times the 12 enrolled students, replacing the class instead of increasing it, although the question says enrollment increased by 5 times the existing students, so the original 12 are dropped before all later additions and departures.

The response multiplies the 600 meters walked in an hour by 24 hours per day, although the question says Lisa walks for only one hour each day, so it treats her as walking around the clock and inflates the two-day distance.

The response correctly finds a net loss of a quarter pool over 3 hours, but subtracts 0.25 pool directly from 120 liters without converting the fraction into liters, and concludes the water level is unchanged, mixing incompatible units.

The response correctly expresses first-round knockouts as 20% of the knockouts, which are half of 190 fights, but never evaluates this second step and reports 95, the total number of knockouts, instead of the first-round subset asked for.

The response correctly lists the deductions as one third and 8% of the $450 salary plus $50, $20 and $10, but never evaluates them and reports 340, a remainder inconsistent with subtracting its own deductions from 450.

The response converts picking 300 cherries in 2 hours into a rate of 300 cherries per hour, doubling the true picking rate, and it also treats the 3 hours needed to make the syrup as 3 hours per quart, multiplying it by 9.

The response restates that four chocolate bars cost as much as 8 magazines but then prices only four magazines, replacing 8 with 4, so the cost of four chocolate bars and hence each bar's price are half of what the stated equivalence implies.

The response correctly derives the capacity of a single red, blue and black boxcar but sums just one of each, never multiplying by the 3 red, 4 blue and 7 black boxcars that the train pulls, so the counts of boxcars are ignored.

The response computes red-hatted small-nosed gnomes by subtracting the blue-hatted small-nosed gnomes from the 21 red-hatted gnomes, mixing two disjoint categories, instead of subtracting the red-hatted big-nosed gnomes obtained from the 14 big-nosed gnomes minus the 6 blue-hatted ones.

The response computes the working time from 8 AM to noon as 8 hours, although noon is four hours after 8 AM, so the available time is doubled and the required number of pieces of laundry per hour comes out half as large.

The response correctly counts 500 flowers across the 20 centerpieces but then prices all 500 flowers as roses and again all 500 as lilies, instead of pricing 10 roses and 15 lilies per centerpiece, so every flower is charged twice at both prices.

The response notes that 200 additional people means two groups of 100, but then calls the increase from 200 to 400 people only 100 additional people and halves the 500 km/hr speed once instead of twice.

The response sets the first leg equal to half of the 40-mile third leg, although the question says the 40 miles is half of the first leg, reversing the relation so the first leg is a quarter of its intended length, and every later leg inherits the error.

The response subtracts a single 1-hour cooldown from 13 hours, although the car must cool down after every 5 hours of driving, and then adds the first 5 hours' 40 miles to the distance for 12 more driving hours, counting those 5 hours twice.

The response correctly counts 64 dog nails and 48 parrot claws, but for the parrot with an extra toe it subtracts 4 claws from the total instead of adding the single extra claw, so the extra toe lowers the count instead of raising it by one.

The response correctly derives 14 subjects for Marius and 17 for Millie from Monica's 10, but evaluates 10 + 14 + 17 as 31, an addition error of ten, and also opens with an unexplained final-answer line of 34.

The response correctly totals 401 books sold over the weekend but then adds the sold books to the 743 books in stock and the 160 received, and later subtracts 743, so books sold increase the inventory instead of being removed from it.

The response explains that a 3:2 payout returns $3 for every $2 bet, but then writes the $60 payout as the bet times 3 instead of the bet times 3/2, dropping the 2 in the ratio so the computed bet is too small.

The response correctly finds the street area and the threefold forest area of 30000 square meters and multiplies by 4 trees per square meter, but evaluates 30000 times 4 as 12000, dropping a factor of ten in the final multiplication.

The response correctly expresses the percentage as 8 pushups divided by the total of 12, 8 and 20 exercises, times 100, but never evaluates it and reports 40.0, which equals the total number of exercises rather than the pushup percentage.

The response subtracts a single month's natural growth of 1/3 inch from the 6 inches needed, although Alex grows 1/3 inch every month for the whole year, then evaluates 6 minus 1/3 as 1/3 and never spreads the hanging time over twelve months.

The response represents one third more guests by multiplying 75 by 1.33, a rounded factor, instead of adding exactly one third of 75, which yields a fractional 99.75 guests and a fractional total number of towels, impossible for counts of people.

The response multiplies the friend's 100 marbles by the 10-marble bet to get 1000 marbles wagered, a quantity unrelated to the 9 games played, and then concludes that Reggie lost 91 games, more games than were played at all.

The response correctly writes the price as 50 bags at $5 plus 50 bags at $7 minus a 10% discount, but never evaluates these expressions and reports 395, both at the start and the end, a value inconsistent with its own setup.

The response correctly tracks 11 ripe peaches after five days but computes the unripe ones as 18 minus 11, which counts the 3 eaten peaches as still unripe in the bowl, instead of subtracting all 14 peaches that ripened from the original 18.

The response applies the 50% increase only once to the 200 students and labels that year as the current one, although three years separate the starting year from this year, so two of the three yearly increases are dropped; its own later verification values are ignored.

The response computes the cooling time from the initial 60 degrees instead of the 240-degree temperature reached after heating, gets a negative time from 60 minus 170, and then takes its absolute value, so the cooling covers the wrong temperature interval.

The response represents the backward shot as a negative velocity and subtracts it from the forward 420, so the result adds the two speeds together, although the question asks how much faster the forward bullet moves, which compares the speeds 420 and 380.

The response computes Mark's reading speed by dividing the 100 pages he read in his former 2-hour day by the new 5 hours, mixing old pages with new time, so the pages-per-hour rate and the weekly total are understated.

The response divides the daily 42-mile round trip by 5 days, as if it were a weekly distance, although the carpool drives 42 miles every commuting day, so the monthly mileage, gallons and gas cost per person are all five times too small.

The response assumes Andrena started with no dolls and counts only Debelyn's gift, never adding Christel's 5 dolls, then transfers the stated relation of Andrena having 2 more dolls than Christel onto Debelyn, instead of using Christel's 19 dolls plus 2 for Andrena.

The response treats the 80% that Jan pays as the discount and subtracts it from the $360 total, so it reports the remaining 20% of the price instead of the 80% share the question says he actually pays.

The response computes the weekly cost from the three $0.50 weekday editions only and omits the $2.00 Sunday edition that Hillary also buys each week, so one recurring purchase is missing from the weekly cost and from the 8-week total.

The response correctly identifies the amount spent as half of the savings, but then computes the remaining balance as its answer although the question asks how much Donny spent; it also evaluates 15 plus 28 plus 13 as 76 and half of it as 46.

The response correctly sets up absent students as 28 times 2/7 and present students as total minus absent, then prints two final lines, the second of which is the number of absent students, so its last reported answer is the absent count rather than the present count.

The response multiplies the 20 minutes per dog by 30 days for only one dog and never multiplies by the 2 dachshunds Jennifer grooms each day, so the daily grooming time and the 30-day total in hours are half of what the question implies.
